 Jaime Jaquez Jr. faces murky future with Milwaukee Bucks after crucial contract decision
 By Jordan Samar October 21, 2026 No Comments 3 Mins Read

 Jaime Jaquez Jr. was part of the massive haul the Milwaukee Bucks got from the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade this summer. The 25-year-old UCLA product didn’t get his rookie-scale extension during Monday’s deadline, so he is essentially entering his contract year.
 The former No. 18 pick will earn roughly $5.9 million this year before becoming a restricted free agent next summer. Jaquez could use the 2026-27 NBA season to prove his worth to the Milwaukee Bucks, who are rebuilding after the blockbuster Antetokounmpo trade.
 Jaime Jaquez Jr.’s Milwaukee Bucks Media Day comment resurfaces amid contract talks 
 Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Milwaukee Bucks forward Jaime Jaquez Jr. (24) brings the ball up court during the second quarter at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images 
 During Media Day last month, Jaime Jaquez Jr. said his approach to his work won’t change, even as he enters his contract year. The former Sixth Man of the Year candidate is fully buying into the franchise’s long-term project.
 “I’d say I approach it the same way I approach every day: just trying to be professional as I can be. I’m here to work right now. My contract is the one that’s going into next year. That’s really the only one I can really worry about… Whatever happens, will happen,” Jaquez stated. 
 Milwaukee Bucks GM made a reassuring vow to Jaime Jaquez Jr. 
 Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Milwaukee Bucks forward Jaime Jaquez Jr. (24) guards Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller (24) during the third quarter at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images 
 Moreover, Bucks general manager Jon Horst reiterated last month that he’ll give everyone a chance to prove themselves, including Jaime Jaquez Jr. During Media Day, he emphasized that the players they received from the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade are not merely throw-ins.
 “We targeted these guys for a reason. We value them significantly. And we’ll, in good faith and sincerely, engage in those conversations,” Horst said. “But we may or may not do an extension, and that’s OK. Just because we don’t doesn’t mean we don’t value them. Those are opportunities for them and for us.”
